exposure: heat-inactivated genital mycoplasmas (Ureaplasma urealyticum, Mycoplasma hominis)
combination of genital mycoplasmas and Gardnerella vaginalis
cohort: The participants were human fetal membranes.
finding: G. vaginalis sustains a proinflammatory response in fetal membranes in vitro, while genital mycoplasmas induce a strong control of the inflammatory response.
